title: The same three letters sort in a different order in German than in Swedish
assumption: Locale-aware sorting just fixes the "accents sort wrong" problem the same way for every language.

input.description: A single sort function applied to the same three-letter list, parameterized only by a BCP 47 locale tag — e.g. a user-preference-driven "sort my contacts" feature.

what_goes_wrong: localeCompare with locale "de" (German) sorts the list as ["a", "\u00e4", "z"] — ä treated as a minor variant of a, placed right next to it. localeCompare with locale "sv" (Swedish) sorts the exact same list as ["a", "z", "\u00e4"] — ä treated as its own letter, placed after z. There is no single "correct" locale-aware order; it depends entirely on which locale you pass.
why: German collation in CLDR (the data behind ICU and JavaScript's Intl) uses the Unicode default ordering with no tailoring: ä is an a with an accent difference, so it sorts right next to a, which matches German dictionary order (DIN 5007-1). CLDR also has a German phonebook variant (de-u-co-phonebk) that sorts ä as "ae". Swedish treats å, ä and ö as separate letters at the end of the alphabet, after z, and the Swedish CLDR collation tailors them there. Both are correct for their own language; a collator has to be told which one to use through its locale argument, and a wrong or missing locale applies one language's rules to another's text. Python's sorted() in the repro is plain code-point order, which happens to agree with Swedish here only because ä (U+00E4) is numerically after z.
fix: Always pass the user's actual locale to the collator rather than relying on a default; never assume one European locale's alphabetical order generalizes to another's. JavaScript ships this via Intl.Collator/localeCompare with a locale argument; Python's standard library has no bundled Unicode collation tables, so matching this behavior requires the system's installed locale data (unreliable across machines) or a third-party ICU binding.

sources.title: Unicode Technical Standard #10: Unicode Collation Algorithm
